[RequireExplicitImplementation]
	public interface INotifyActorDisposing { void Disposing(Actor self); }

manual_source_reviewed_facts.meaning: WillDispose and Disposed are distinct. Actor.Dispose first invokes CurrentActivity?.OnActorDisposeOuter(this); only if control proceeds does it set WillDispose=true and enqueue. There is no whole-method early Disposed guard. Do not promise entire Dispose is idempotent or thread-safe.

The queued lambda checks Disposed and returns if already true. Otherwise it conditionally calls World.Remove(this) when IsInWorld, invokes Disposing on selected INotifyActorDisposing traits, calls World.TraitDict.RemoveActor(this), sets Disposed=true, then invokes luaInterface?.Value.OnActorDestroyed(). Written order depends on prior operations returning normally.

TraitsImplementing<T> delegates to World.TraitDict.WithInterface<T>(this). INotifyActorDisposing declares Disposing(Actor self). Internal lookup/removal and concrete callbacks are dependencies not fully verified by this selection.

World.Remove(Actor) sets IsInWorld=false, removes ActorID from actors, invokes ActorRemoved, then notifies INotifyRemovedFromWorld traits. No guarantee all notifications complete if a callback throws.

frameEndActions is declared Queue<Action<World>>. AddFrameEndTask only enqueues its action; it does not execute it. There is no explicit locking or generic cleanup guarantee in this selected declaration.

World.Tick has a Paused/shellmap condition around actor/trait/effect update work. The while(frameEndActions.Count != 0) Dequeue()(this) loop is outside that condition. If Tick reaches the loop, pause alone does not skip it; this does not guarantee Tick is called or callbacks finish.

The loop tests the live queue count each iteration, not a frozen snapshot. New tasks enqueued by callbacks can be processed before that drain ends if execution continues. No promised next-frame-only timing, termination, exception recovery or universal task completion.

World.Dispose sets Disposing=true, deactivates the order generator if present, and clears already queued frame-end work before calling a.Dispose() over actors.Values.Reverse(). It then drains newly queued tasks, conditionally disposes the shellmap OrderManager, disposes Map and finishes benchmark. This differs from guaranteeing every earlier queued task runs.

Selected callback and drain paths have no explicit exception recovery/finally that guarantees all remaining disposal operations. Flag comments about race prevention do not establish synchronization. No source or game program was executed.

Repository test path metadata includes ActionQueueTest.cs and ActorInfoTest.cs. No direct actor/frame-end lifecycle test body or passing result is supplied here. State that limit; do not invent test names/coverage/results. Use a short exact source fragment as an example, explicitly not a complete compiled/run program. No full engine, game loop caller, trait dictionary or activity/Lua dependency contract is proven.

required_faq_questions.en: Does Actor.Dispose immediately set Disposed=true or make every repeated call a complete no-op?
required_faq_questions.pt-BR: Actor.Dispose define Disposed=true imediatamente ou torna toda chamada repetida uma operação totalmente sem efeito?
required_faq_questions.expected: No: immediate hook/WillDispose phase differs from guarded delayed Disposed phase; earlier work may repeat.

required_faq_questions.en: Does Paused by itself prevent World.Tick from draining frame-end tasks?
required_faq_questions.pt-BR: Paused, por si só, impede World.Tick de processar a fila de fim de frame?
required_faq_questions.expected: No: the loop is outside the update gate if execution reaches it, without universal completion guarantee.

required_faq_questions.en: Does World.Dispose guarantee execution of tasks queued before it started?
required_faq_questions.pt-BR: World.Dispose garante a execução de tarefas enfileiradas antes de começar?
required_faq_questions.expected: No: it clears the old queue before actor disposal/new drain; exceptions/cleanup completion remain unverified.

complete_review_groups_required: Delayed operation order and normal-completion qualifiers
Live queue and no fixed next-frame/universal guarantee
World shutdown clears old queue and drains new actor disposal work
Source-shaped labelled example and honest absence of direct test results
